entries.desc: After a current signed reviewer pass, each registered closeout artifact writer records integrity-chained cooperative local-runtime lineage with a registered writer label; when only bounded story metadata intervenes, the existing reviewer receipt remains mechanically fresh, while specialized artifact gates independently validate schema, digest, reviewer, policy, command-set, and freshness facts. Hostile same-UID repository/runtime modification is an explicit non-goal unless a future isolated trust domain is configured.

evidence.command: npm run test:closeout-trust && npm run test:process-fact-contract
evidence.note: Cooperative local-runtime lineage preserves review freshness; specialized gate validators remain independent and hostile same-UID authority is not claimed.

entries.desc: A normal sequence containing several different registered closeout writers preserves the same review round and reviewer receipt across every intermediate HEAD, and the freshness result exposes an auditable trusted-metadata-descendant reason rather than silently weakening hash checks.

evidence.note: Multi-writer closeout retains the review round across bounded metadata descendants.

entries.desc: Repeated idempotent writes of the same canonical artifact and a trusted modify-then-revert metadata history remain retainable only when every intervening commit/path is classified by the shared canonical lineage evaluator.

evidence.note: Repeated writes, replay, modify-revert, and causal chains remain bounded.

entries.desc: Concurrent HEAD movement between lineage evaluation and artifact persistence is detected with a before/after HEAD check and refuses retention; a stable retry can then succeed without corrupting the prior receipt.

evidence.note: Stable before/after HEAD is required; concurrent movement refuses retention.

entries.desc: Legacy closeout evidence lacking the new writer envelope is handled by an explicit compatibility/refusal disposition and never implicitly promoted to trusted lineage.

evidence.command: npm run test:closeout-trust && npm run test:process-fact-contract
evidence.note: Legacy/missing lineage is not promoted and dead pseudo-authority helpers remain absent.

entries.desc: The shared writer contract is consumed by every listed closeout artifact producer, and a consumer matrix proves every production gate uses its specialized validator rather than treating review-retention lineage as artifact approval.

evidence.note: Producer and specialized consumer matrix is mechanically checked.

entries.desc: Any source-code or story-owned material drift invalidates reviewer receipt retention even when surrounded by trusted metadata commits.

evidence.note: Source and story-owned material drift invalidates retention.

entries.desc: Configuration, validation policy, or validation command-set/order drift invalidates retention and reports the exact changed binding.

evidence.note: Material/story/scope/round bindings reject real drift.

entries.desc: An unknown, misspelled, or non-registered writer label is rejected fail-closed inside the cooperative local-runtime boundary and cannot be laundered through a trusted metadata path.

evidence.note: Unknown and non-registered labels fail the cooperative boundary.

entries.desc: Direct/manual artifact mutation without current coherent lineage invalidates retention even if content resembles a registered artifact; coherent hostile same-UID forgery remains an explicitly tested non-goal, not a claim of durable authority.

evidence.note: Manual incoherent mutation fails; coherent hostile same-UID forgery is explicitly exercised as a non-goal, not durable authority.

entries.desc: Malformed, unverifiable, non-ancestor, cyclic, or incoherent lineage data is rejected fail-closed with no reviewer-pass carry-forward.

evidence.note: Malformed, reordered, copied, non-ancestor, and incoherent lineage fails closed.

entries.desc: A registered writer may not whitelist arbitrary dirty paths: user files, source, config, command entrypoints, and unregistered metadata remain untrusted.

evidence.command: npm run test:closeout-trust && npm run test:process-fact-contract
evidence.note: Unregistered paths remain untrusted and gates do not consume receipt lineage as approval.

entries.desc: Changing only headHash is insufficient for retention unless exact-head or fully verified trusted-metadata-descendant lineage plus unchanged material/storyFiles/policy/command-set bindings is proven.

evidence.note: Lifecycle retention requires unchanged material/story/scope/round and stable metadata lineage; prior focused lifecycle check remains applicable because F-008/F-011 do not modify retention consumers.

entries.desc: Starting with one current complete REVIEW round, the standard unattended REVIEW→TEST→DONE path produces routine validation evidence, delivery check, summary, live-smoke transcript, DONE-required evidence, and a PASS done_prepare report, then reaches DONE with zero metadata-only DEV/REVIEW backsteps, zero extra reviewer re-attestations, zero human confirmations, and zero re-execution of an unchanged validation command set.

evidence.note: One-pass closeout and durable convergence telemetry pass with zero-cost claims derived from actual event history.

evidence.note: Machine-readable counters derive phase, validation, review, and human facts; pre-TEST re-attestation is now non-zero.

entries.desc: Delivery reviewer dispatch and delivery_check_set have the same mechanically enforced legal phase/cardinality; dispatching and writing in that phase succeeds, while the prompt never instructs an action the handler rejects.

evidence.note: Delivery reviewer dispatch/writer phase contract remains aligned.

entries.desc: A fresh unchanged routine validation or DONE-required receipt is reused through the canonical evaluator and records disposition=reused with commandExecutions=0; an explicit validate:false remains a distinct skipped/not-run state and cannot masquerade as reuse or PASS.

evidence.note: Fresh validation/DONE-required reuse remains bounded and zero-execution semantics are preserved.

entries.desc: Each trusted closeout write performed after review preserves the current reviewer receipt through canonical lineage, including multiple metadata commits and an immediate idempotent done_prepare retry.

evidence.note: Trusted closeout metadata lineage preserves review freshness across multiple writes.

entries.desc: A closeout retry after a classified infrastructure interruption resumes from durable fresh artifacts without duplicating reviewer work, human acknowledgement, or unchanged commands.

evidence.note: Interrupted closeout recovery remains bounded and does not duplicate reviewer work.

entries.desc: The ordered closeout transaction remains deterministic when optional live-smoke or DONE-required policy is disabled: omitted phases are explicitly not-applicable and budgets/counts include only enabled phases.

evidence.note: Missing or incomplete convergence facts omit the cosmetic zero claim.

evidence.note: Durable closeout telemetry remains registered as gate-consumed process facts.

evidence.note: Real material and unsafe-path drift remain fail-closed.

evidence.note: True validation failure and timeout remain blocking terminals.

evidence.note: Duplicate unchanged execution and reused-with-execution violate convergence.

entries.desc: Writing summary, transcript, delivery, validation, or DONE-required artifacts in any permutation not admitted by the canonical ordering cannot invalidate receipts and then silently bounce to DEV/REVIEW; it must either be normalized by the shared writer or rejected with a bounded next action.

evidence.note: Collector regression proves REVIEW-anchor re-attestation before TEST is counted while old rounds are excluded.

entries.desc: No convergence breaker/human-ack path is entered solely because trusted closeout metadata advanced HEAD; a test fails if any human:true resume/ack command is requested in the positive closeout transcript.

evidence.note: Human acknowledgement and validation terminals remain durable typed facts.

entries.desc: Editing only the body of an existing exported function while preserving its declaration identity/signature is classified as modified, not deleted; concept preflight does not emit a deleted-symbol blocker for buildQueryGroups, candidateReadBindingErrors, defaultHostRunRunner, or equivalent declarations.

evidence.note: Observed TypeScript body-only edits remain modifications, not deletions.

entries.desc: Removing a declaration (or changing it so its prior declaration identity/signature truly disappears) is classified as a true deletion, and remaining imports/calls/references produce the existing residual-reference blocker.

evidence.note: True TypeScript and multiline Python declaration deletion remains detected.

entries.desc: Body-only edits that add/remove nested control-flow blocks, local variables, callbacks, object properties, or semantic anchors do not affect the enclosing declaration identity.

evidence.note: Nested body/control-flow edits preserve enclosing declaration identity.

entries.desc: Whitespace, comments, formatting, generic/type annotation changes that preserve the configured signature identity, and moving a declaration within the same file follow an explicit stable classification rather than regex-anchor disappearance.

evidence.note: Signature replacements and multiline Python header identity are deterministic.

entries.desc: Supported declaration forms—exported/non-exported function declarations, const/arrow functions, async/generator functions, class methods, constructors, and overload declarations—are matched by syntax-aware declaration identity with deterministic handling of duplicate names/scopes.

evidence.note: Functions, methods, constructors, overloads, Python multiline def/class, and scoped duplicates are covered.

entries.desc: A deliberate rename is represented as old-symbol deletion plus new-symbol addition (or an explicit rename relation) and still checks residual references to the old declaration.

evidence.note: Renames and export removal remain detectable declaration identity changes.

entries.desc: An identifier with the deleted symbol name appearing only in comments, strings, nested locals, object keys, or an unrelated scope cannot satisfy declaration-presence or suppress a true deletion.

evidence.note: Comments, strings, and unrelated scopes cannot forge declaration survivors.

entries.desc: A declaration retained but made unreachable, unexported, or signature-incompatible is not blindly accepted as body-only; the classifier reports the actual identity/export/signature change and applies the appropriate blocker.

evidence.note: Export/signature incompatibility remains fail-closed rather than body-only.

entries.desc: Deleting one of multiple same-name declarations or overloads is detected by file/scope/kind/signature identity rather than hidden by another declaration with the same text name.

evidence.note: Same-name overload multiplicity and cross-file scope remain explicit identities.

entries.desc: Parser failure, malformed source, unsupported syntax, or ambiguous declaration identity fails closed with a typed diagnostic; it must not silently report no deletion or fall back to the old semantic-anchor false-positive regex.

evidence.note: Malformed TypeScript plus malformed/unterminated multiline Python headers emit diagnostics and concept FAIL.

entries.desc: The regression corpus contains paired fixtures for body-only modification versus true declaration deletion using the three symbols observed in B-3aec, and asserts both no false positive and no false negative/residual-reference regression.

evidence.note: Combined corpus now includes observed false positives, true deletions, cross-file collisions, overloads, and multiline Python regressions.
